# Decode separator-intersection lattices

Use when a large ARC grid has regular horizontal/vertical separator lines with mostly uniform background along the lines, while small colored values appear at crossings. The output may be a compressed matrix over adjacent lattice faces.

## Verified evidence from task-47246f29

Three supplied demonstrations decode exactly by reading colored values at successive separator intersections. For each output cell, inspect the four corner crossing values from a 2x2 block of adjacent intersections: if all four crossing values are the same, output that color; otherwise output the interior panel/background color (3 in the demonstrated examples).

Demo 3 gives a clear cell-by-cell check. Lattice crossing rows are 8,13,18,23,28 and columns 4,9,14,19,24,29. Output is the 4x5 matrix for adjacent pairs of crossing rows/columns. E.g. the top-left 2x2 crossing block is all 0, so output 0; the next is all 0; mixed corners map to panel background 3; the bottom-right all-4 block maps to 4. This reproduces all 20 output cells. Demo 1 similarly produces a 4x6 matrix; demo 2's all-uniform lattice decodes to a single 8.

## Region selection resolved on task-47246f29

Do not assume a universal marker-only crop rule. Form faces between consecutive separator-crossing rows and columns, but use demos to determine the lattice span and whether edge crossings are included. Mixed corner colors map to the panel/interior background; unanimous four corners map to that shared color.

Fresh demo/test sequence validates full edge-inclusive lattice extent. Demo grid 27x23 had horizontal separator rows 1,4,7,10,13,16,19,22,25 and vertical separator columns 1,8,15,22. Crop crossings to rows 4..22 and cols 1..22, yielding 6x3 faces, with mixed cells becoming background 8. Test grid 24x28 had separator rows 0,5,10,15,20 and columns 0,6,12,18,24. The edge-inclusive lattice produced 4x4 faces, mixed cells background 2, and unanimous corners copied. Accepted output:
`[[2,2,2,7],[6,2,2,2],[2,2,2,2],[2,1,2,8]]`.

Older examples for this task showed other marker-based cropping; treat crop boundaries as instance-dependent and infer them from geometry plus demos, rather than assuming standout marker colors alone define the span.

## Additional confirmed cropped-lattice variant (task-47246f29)

A fresh instance supplied two demos and a 24x28 test. The accepted output is the 5x6 matrix
`[[1,1,1,4,1,3],[5,1,4,1,1,1],[5,1,1,1,8,1],[1,1,1,1,8,8],[4,1,7,1,8,1]]`.

For this test, use horizontal colored-crossing rows 7,10,13,16,19,22 and vertical colored-crossing columns 3,7,11,15,19,23,27 (0-indexed). The selected crossing lattice is therefore 6x7, producing 5x6 faces. For each output cell, inspect the four crossing colors at the corners of that face: if all four are identical, copy that color; otherwise use the interior/panel color 1. This reproduces every accepted output cell, including unanimous 4,3,5,8,7 regions and mixed-corner cells→1. The crop is not the full visible grid: omit earlier blank separator rows and begin at the first horizontal row with colored lattice-crossings (row 7); the crossing columns begin at 3 and include the rightmost crossing at 27.

Demo 2 (26x29) independently confirms the rule and mixed-cell color. Its crossing rows were 1,9,17,25 and columns 3,9,15,21,27; four-corner unanimity/mixed→interior 7 gives the demonstrated 3x4 output `[[1,1,7,5],[7,7,7,7],[2,2,7,0]]`. The test output was finally accepted after three wrong submissions. Those failed attempts incorrectly included the unused upper lattice rows and/or extra crossing columns, and manually mis-copied several corner-consensus cells; the accepted output used precisely the 5x6 crop above. Thus dimensions/crop are as important as the consensus rule.

A separate first demo (23x29) has output 5x4 and appears broadly consistent with adjacent-crossing consensus, but at least one adjacent face with four 0 corners appears as 9 in the provided output. Do not force that demo into an unqualified rule; re-audit crossing coordinates, crop, and any selection condition cell-by-cell. This task family has known variable crops/variants. On recurrence, derive selected crossing rows/columns from the actual demos, compute each four-corner block explicitly, verify every output cell and dimensions, and do not guess a full visible lattice.

## Further verified variant evidence (task-47246f29)

A fresh stream instance (30x26) had background interior color 1, separator/background color 3, and a 9-valued lattice at separator crossings. The rows with horizontal separator bands were 4,12,20,28; the vertical lattice crossing columns were 1,8,15,22. The bottom horizontal band at row 28 had no 9-valued vertices, and the rightmost crossing column at 22 only appears in the upper lattice rows. Five demos in the same task family showed multiple varying output shapes (4x5, 2x4, 4x2, 5x3, 5x3), so output crop is not universally the full face lattice.

Two submissions of plausible full-lattice consensus-derived 3x3 outputs were wrong. The accepted output for this test was exactly 2x3:
`[[9,9,9],[1,9,1]]`.

Implications: do not infer a full rectangular output merely from all adjacent separator intervals. Demonstrations must establish which lattice rows/columns/regions are retained, and test variants may use a truncated or selected crop. Mixed cells in demos often map to the panel interior color, but never assume that the final output dimensions cover the entire visible separator lattice. Respect both the marker/lattice inclusion boundaries and edge omissions; when no precise crop is established, request a targeted demo instead of trying a likely-looking full output.

## Additional verified instance evidence (same task family)

A 21x29 demo had a 5-valued marker at the first four consecutive horizontal/vertical separator crossings along the top and lower boundary; these selected crossings defined a 1x3 output of all 5s. The remaining separators/crossings outside that selected span were not included. In a corresponding 30x30 test, the only selected crossings were color 4 at rows 0 and 27 and columns 4 and 24, yielding one face and the accepted output `[[4]]`. Thus when a sparse set of same-valued corner markers delimits a crop, form faces between consecutive selected crossing rows/columns; do not extend the output across the unmarked intervening separator lattice. Four matching corner values for the selected face yield that value.

## Further confirmed sparse-boundary crop variant (task-47246f29)

A fresh instance test was 14x28 with panel color 8 and separator color 5. Colored crossing markers occurred on horizontal separator rows 0, 4, and 8 at vertical crossing columns 0, 8, 16, and 24; row 12 was a separator but had no colored crossing markers. The accepted output was 2x3:
`[[1,8,4],[8,8,4]]`.

Use only the consecutive marker-bearing crossing rows/columns as the selected lattice; do not include a following blank separator row. For each adjacent selected crossing rectangle, output the shared color when all four corners agree, otherwise panel color 8. This yields first row `[1,8,4]` and second row `[8,8,4]`. A first attempt incorrectly included the unmarked row-12 boundary and predicted a 3x3 result; accepted dimensions confirm that unmarked outer separators do not extend the crop in this variant.

## Method

1. Locate repeating full separator rows/columns and list their intersection coordinates.
2. Derive candidate output dimensions from adjacent intersections/faces, but test whether boundary rows/columns are clipped or only a subset is selected.
3. For each candidate face, read its four crossing colors. Compare uniform corners versus mixed corners; mixed faces may map to the panel background.
4. Replay the entire candidate output against every demo, including dimensions, before applying it.
5. If a test disagrees despite exact demo replay, treat it as evidence of an unmodeled selection or clipping rule; do not repeat near-identical outputs. Strict action interface: one JSON action only.

# Reconstruct periodic pattern from tiled panel

Use when an ARC grid contains a small patch of arbitrary colored cells embedded in a mostly uniform area, with horizontal/vertical separator lines forming a regular larger lattice or repeated blocks.

## Verified task-8e04f0ad instance

A 15x20 demo had color-4 separators at row 7 and columns 6 and 13. In the lower-right 6x6 panel (rows 8..13, cols 14..19), the 5x6 colored motif was surrounded by color-8 background. Output replicated that panel's entire 6x6 contents periodically across each 6x6 region of the whole grid, including on both sides of the separators and above/below the horizontal separator. Precisely, periodic indexing mapped output[r][c] from the motif at local coordinates `(r-8) mod 6, (c-14) mod 6`; source background color 8 was preserved, and the source's final row (all 8s) was included. Copy that complete 4x9 left-block pattern periodically into the right block, preserving the separators, with no extra transformation. Precisely, the entire 4x9 left block pattern copied to columns 10..18, with row alignment unchanged. General approach: detect the repeated template cell dimensions from separator coordinates and adjacent panels; apply modulo indexing to copy source template into corresponding regions, keeping separator lines intact. Do not assume source panel is the bottom-right in future variants; use the demo to identify which region contains the pattern and the exact tile period/orientation.

# ARC grid rule inference under action constraints

Use this class-level workflow for ARC/Continual-ARC puzzles with demonstrations and a limited number of submissions or demo requests.

## Confirmed task-518fa031: tile input into a 2x2 array of rotations
Three demonstrations and accepted tests establish: double both input dimensions by placing four copies in quadrants. Top-left = original. Top-right = 90° clockwise rotation. Bottom-left = 90° counterclockwise rotation. Bottom-right = 180° rotation. This is exact full-grid tiling; no recoloring or other changes. Verify each quadrant mechanically against the demos, then assert output shape is (2H)x(2W). In the 3x3 demo, input [[6,7,7],[6,7,7],[7,6,7]] produced the stated arrangement, confirming quadrant orientations. Accepted tests include 6x6→12x12 (binary 0/5 grid, confirming the rule on the present recurrence), 15x15→30x30 with values 1/4, and 30x30 output. Earlier attempts were rejected because of mistaken quadrant/orientation transcription, despite the correct broad hypothesis; use programmatic transforms and compare demos cell-for-cell rather than manually composing quadrants. The 8x8 demo explicitly matches TL input, TR CW, BL CCW, BR 180.

### Known pitfall: orientation implementation
For `cw(A)`, output row r is input column `H-1-r` read top-to-bottom. For `ccw(A)`, output row r is input column `r` read bottom-to-top. The correct Python functions validated against demos are:
`cw = [list(row) for row in zip(*A[::-1])]`
`ccw = [list(row) for row in zip(*A)][::-1]`
`rot180 = [row[::-1] for row in A[::-1]]`
Put each corresponding row-quadrant beside each other, and stack the two quadrant rows. Verify with the demos before submission. Beware superficially similar transpose/rotation implementations: in this run three attempted grids were rejected because transcription/computation did not match the intended quadrant mapping, whereas the verified transforms were accepted.

## Task-518fa031 earlier unresolved note (superseded)
A prior instance had been incorrectly labeled unresolved after eight wrong attempts on a 6x6 test; later recurrence has now confirmed the actual 2x2 rotation rule. Discard the earlier unresolved claim and use the confirmed rule above on recurrence, while validating the current demos and orientation mappings.


## Confirmed panel-template replication variant: task-8e04f0ad
Full-width/full-height separator lines of color 9 partition the grid into equal rectangular panels. One panel contains a pattern and the other panels are blank/background; copy the source panel's pattern into every panel at the same local coordinates, preserving separator lines. Infer panel height/width from separator spacing and identify the uniquely populated source region; do not copy separator cells as part of the pattern. Demo: 6x26 with vertical color-4 separators at columns 8 and 17; the 6x8 pattern in the first panel repeated at local coordinates in the next two panels, while separator columns remained 4. Accepted test: 20x19 with color-9 separator rows 6 and 13 and column 9, dividing into 3x2 panels of 6x9 interior cells; the populated bottom-left 6x9 tile was copied into all six panels at matching local coordinates, leaving row/column separator lines unchanged. Preserve all copied colors, including 0, and preserve background cells within the source tile.

## Infer and verify
1. Parse dimensions, colors, candidate background/edge colors, markers, and action caps. Index cells consistently by row and column.
2. Compare each demo input/output at identical coordinates. Enumerate changed cells, their original and output colors, and unchanged structures. Separate marker recoloring from rays/fills and from wholesale stripe changes.
3. Maintain a small set of plausible rules. Consider orientation, anchor, extent, endpoint exclusion, target colors, and object interaction separately; do not infer from a single visual resemblance.
4. Replay every candidate on every demo cell-by-cell. Reject any rule that misses a changed cell or alters a preserved cell. A transformation is not validated merely because one part fits.
5. Apply the surviving rule to the test input, preserve unrelated cells, and validate dimensions, row lengths, bounds, and palette before submission.

## Demo/action budget
- A request costs score. Request only when a concrete ambiguity remains and explain internally which candidate rules the next example should distinguish.
- Use only actions authorized by the puzzle interface. In a submit/request_demos/finish protocol, do not call unrelated tools or task-planning actions; reason from visible grids and output only the required JSON action.
- After incorrect feedback, do not submit a near-identical grid with superficial edits. Treat the candidate rule as suspect, identify which assumptions were unproven, and reconstruct the output from the demos.
- If demos leave a behavior unresolved, do not present it as established. Seek a discriminating example only if worth its cost; otherwise make the most evidence-supported choice within the remaining attempt budget.

## Directional lines and boundary rays
For markers near edge bars, verify independently: ray direction, whether the marker becomes the ray color or a special color, where the ray stops, whether the boundary is preserved, and whether only marker-containing rows/columns activate. For diagonal rays, check each next cell: a current task-9bc5df6e run had rays extend through background to the boundary, but a test ray's next cell was a foreign non-background color and the accepted output preserved that blocker and added no ray. Thus use background-only extension when supported and never overwrite foreign-color cells without demo evidence. Other task-9bc5df6e recurrences had rays reaching boundaries; treat variant scope carefully. Do not assume opposite-edge symmetry. Special complete bands or stripes may have a separate selection rule; preserve them unless demonstrations establish how they are selected. See `references/boundary-ray-case.md` for a documented example and its limitations.

### Additional accepted blocker-sensitive no-op recurrence (7x24 test)
Three demos and the accepted test establish: extend selected same-color diagonal pairs outward through background, stopping at grid edges or non-background blockers. Demo 1 (9x23, bg1): 5 pair at (4,13),(5,14) extends NW from (4,13) through (3,12),(2,11),(1,10),(0,9); 7 pair at (6,14),(7,13) extends SW from (7,13) to (8,12). Demo 2 (11x23, bg9): 0 pair at (4,2),(5,1) extends up-right from (4,2) through (3,3),(2,4),(1,5),(0,6); 5 pair at (7,2),(8,3) extends down-right from (7,2) through (9,4),(10,5), preserving existing cells. Demo 3 (11x8, bg7) has a tiny adjacent 4/9 and 0 motif with no same-color diagonal pair and is unchanged. Accepted test (7x24, bg2) is exactly unchanged: 7s at (0,5),(1,4) suggest a diagonal, but one direction is out of bounds and the other immediately encounters foreign color 1 at (2,3); preserve blocker and do not continue through it. The 7 at (2,4) is vertical-adjacent, not a diagonal continuation. When all plausible rays are out of bounds or blocked, preserve the entire grid. Note an early guessed ray submission was wrong; unchanged output was accepted after valid-grid submission.

### Additional diagonal-ray run task-9bc5df6e (accepted test; selector nuanced)
A further run had three demos and an accepted 25x6 test. Background-only diagonal rays are supported, but direction and activation must be inferred per motif; do not extend every diagonal pair in both directions.

- Demo 1 (28x20, background 6): preserve the multicolor seed near rows 0–2, cols 7–10. Extend color 7 from (0-indexed row 2,col 7) diagonally down-left through background to (row 9,col 0), and color 4 from (row 2,col 10) diagonally down-right through background to (row 11,col 19). Other cells unchanged.
- Demo 2 (13x15, background 9): preserve seed motif around rows 7–9, cols 11–13. Extend color 6 down-left from (row 9,col 11), adding (10,10),(11,9),(12,8). Other cells unchanged.
- Demo 3 (28x9, background 3): preserve seed at rows 24–26, cols 0–2; extend color 9 up-right from (row 24,col 2), adding (23,3),(22,4),(21,5),(20,6),(19,7),(18,8). Other cells unchanged.
- Accepted test (25x6, background 3): add only color 4 at (0-indexed row 20,col 5), continuing the diagonal from existing color-4 cells (row 21,col 4) and (row 22,col 3). All other cells, including the nearby diagonal color-9 pair, remained unchanged. Several guesses extending color 9 in one or both directions, or extending both colors, were wrong. A diagonal seed alone is insufficient to activate a ray; preserve non-selected/blocked motifs and infer selection from full local motif geometry/context. This run confirms one ray can be selected while a nearby-looking diagonal pair is untouched. Do not infer a broader selector beyond these demos. See also the variant history below.

## Confirmed task-a8c517ee variant: fill enclosed frame interiors by parity
Two demos and an accepted test establish that outlined rectangular/square frames retain their borders while enclosed background cells are filled. The demonstrated outputs show fill color 2 when both interior dimensions are even (demo 2: a 2x2 hole; accepted test: a 6x6 hole), and color 7 when at least one interior dimension is odd (demo 1: 5x5; demo 2: 5x5, 5x7, 1x1, and 3x3; accepted test: 3x3 and 1x1). Another accepted 25x16 test had a 4-frame with a 4x4 interior (filled 2) and a 4-frame with a 5x5 interior (filled 7), confirming same-color frames can receive different fills based on their interior dimensions. Other grid cells and frame borders stay unchanged. This parity mapping fits all observed cases. A further accepted 21x18 recurrence confirmed it: a color-4 frame with a 2x2 interior was filled with 2, while color-1 frame with 5x5 interior and color-8 frame with 1x1 interior were filled with 7; all frame borders and unrelated cells were preserved. Do not fill frame borders or globally recolor frame colors. Accepted test 15x20: the 4-frame at rows 0–7, cols 8–15 has 6x6 interior filled 2; the 5-frame at rows 9–13, cols 10–14 has 3x3 interior filled 7; the 6-frame at rows 10–12, cols 3–5 has its single interior cell filled 7.
